[[Image:Dianthus gratianopolitanus2.jpg|thumb|''Dianthus gratianopolitanus'']]
'''''Dianthus gratianopolitanus''''', commonly known as the '''Cheddar pink''' or '''clove pink''',<ref name = RHSPF/> is a species of plant in the family [[Caryophyllaceae]]. It is a herbaceous perennial, hardy to [[Hardiness zone|zones 4–8]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Dianthus gratianopolitanus (Cheddar Pink) {{!}} North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox|url=https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/dianthus-gratianopolitanus/|access-date=2021-02-22|website=plants.ces.ncsu.edu}}</ref> It grows to a height of 0.5 to 1 feet, blooming from May to June. Flowers are fragrant and rose pink. Grows best in full sun and has medium water requirements. Overwatering or poor drainage leads to crown rot, and plants do not tolerate wet winter soil conditions.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dianthus gratianopolitanus - Plant Finder|url=https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=279029&isprofile=1&basic=dianthus%20gratianopolitanus|access-date=2021-02-22|website=www.missouribotanicalgarden.org}}</ref>

The [[specific epithet]] ''gratianopolitanus'' refers to the ancient Roman name ''Gratianopolis'' of the modern French city of [[Grenoble]].<ref>Dominique Villars. Histoire des plantes de Dauphiné. vol. 3. part 2. 1789. [https://biodiversitylibrary.org/page/50341801]</ref> The common name Cheddar pink refers to the fact that it's native to the [[Cheddar Gorge]] in [[England]].<ref name=":0" />

It is native to western and central [[Europe]], from the UK to [[Ukraine]].<ref name=":0" /> It became a protected species in the UK in 1975 under the Conservation of Wild Creatures and Wild Plants Act.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.caithness.org/caithnessfieldclub/bulletins/1975/october/conservation.htm|title = Caithness CWS - Caithness Field Club - Annual Bulletins - 1975 - October - Conservation}}</ref>

==Cultivation==
[[Cultivars]] include 'Feuerhexe' (syn. 'Fire Witch'), 'Grandiflorus' and 'Tiny Rubies'.<ref>[http://www.perennials.com/plants/dianthus-gratianopolitanus-tiny-rubies.html Heritage Perennials]</ref> ''Dianthus gratianopolitanus'' has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/5722/Dianthus-gratianopolitanus/Details | title = ''Dianthus gratianopolitanus'' | website = www.rhs.org | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | accessdate = 24 February 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 31 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | website = www.rhs.org | accessdate = 18 February 2020}}</ref>
